videos.title: Michael B. Jordan on Being Loved Isn't Enough to Make It Work
videos.description:
Michael B. Jordan spent years feeling guilty about his own success. Now he thinks the guilt was the job description.

In this clip, Michael B. Jordan and Jay Shetty talk about growing up in North New Jersey with two present parents, a house everybody came to, and no idea at the time that the family was broke.

He opens up about the call you can only make to your mom once you're old enough to understand what she carried, the years he couldn't accept a blessing without questioning why it landed on him, and the moment he stopped calling it luck and started calling it a path.

Learn about the chip he got from sharing a name with the greatest ever, what he's obsessed with right now, and the one thing he'd have said years earlier if he wasn't afraid of how people would react.

videos.title: More AI output doesn't produce better product
videos.description: Frontier models have no idea what to ship. The ideas, the prioritization, and the judgment about what the market actually wants still have to come from a human who has talked to customers. Ryan found PMF for Untangle not by shipping more code, but by getting a single meeting with a family law attorney named Renee Bauer and listening.

videos.title: Your coding agent can run your business operations, not just your codebase
videos.description: Claire uses Devin to run deal desk, custom quoting, and customer triage. Ryan uses it for investor updates with a built-in skill. Both treat the question "what would you do with someone who knows your codebase and can write code to solve anything?" as a prompt for finding new uses, not a description of a limited tool.

videos.title: Growth Is a Series of Small Funerals
videos.description: Every version of you that got left behind was doing the best it could with what it knew at the time. Growing up means honoring those people even as you outgrow them.

videos.title: Why Achieving Your Dream Feels Impossible
videos.description: The gap between your dream and today isn't the problem, the missing chain of smaller goals in between is. What's a big goal you finally started moving on once you broke it down small enough?
